title: Best Social Media Marketers (2026): How to Hire a Social Media Manager
description: How to hire a social media marketer: strategy vs content vs management, what a monthly package should include, safe account access, and red flags.
intro: Hiring help with social media can free up hours every week, but 'social media marketing' can mean a one-off strategy, a batch of designed posts, or someone running your accounts every day. This guide helps you decide which one you need and what to expect from it.

faq.q: Should I give a social media manager my password?
faq.a: No. Platforms such as Facebook and Instagram (through Meta Business Suite), LinkedIn pages and scheduling tools let you add people with their own login and limited roles. Remove access when the work ends.

faq.q: Can a marketer guarantee a number of followers?
faq.a: Real growth cannot be guaranteed. Guaranteed follower or like counts usually mean bought or fake engagement, which can hurt your reach and break platform rules.

faq.q: Are paid ads included in social media management?
faq.a: Usually not. Running paid ads is a separate service, and the ad budget itself is paid by you directly to the platform. Check whether ad management is part of the package.

faq.q: How do I measure whether it is working?
faq.a: Agree on a few numbers before starting: reach, engagement rate, profile visits, link clicks, or leads. Ask for a short monthly report comparing them with the previous month.

faq.q: Do I need to approve posts before they go live?
faq.a: You should, at least at first. Ask for a content calendar a week or a month ahead so you can review captions and designs before they are scheduled.
